question: Why did FeCoNiCrMn@CNTs adsorb more 2-CEES than pristine CNTs between 30 min and 30 h?
expect: premise false: in that period its apparent capacity stayed LOWER than pristine CNTs', attributed to concurrent catalytic degradation; it ends higher only at 48 h (636 mg/g) (sec. 3.2)
rendered: According to the document, the apparent adsorption capacity of FeCoNiCrMn@CNTs remained lower than that of pristine CNTs between 30 min and 30 h. This behavior may be attributed to the coexistence of adsorption and catalytic degradation processes. Pure CNTs primarily rely on physical adsorption mechanisms, whereas FeCoNiCrMn nanoparticles introduce multimetallic active sites that can catalyze the chemical transformation of 2-CEES. As a result, part of the adsorbed 2-CEES may undergo catalytic conversion rather than simple accumulation, thereby reducing the net gravimetrically measured mass gain during this period.
